slot.brief: Two springs first connected in series then in parallel to the same mass; compare the ratio of time periods, or a cut-spring variant where a spring is cut into pieces and the new k is found.

stem: A uniform spring of length $L$ and force constant $k$ is cut into pieces of lengths $L/3$ and $2L/3$. With the same mass attached, the pieces are connected first in series and then in parallel, with their other ends fixed. Find $T_{\text{series}}/T_{\text{parallel}}$.

verdicts.working: For a uniform spring, stiffness is inversely proportional to length, so the pieces have constants 3k and 3k/2. Thus k_series = k and k_parallel = 9k/2. Since T = 2π√(m/k_eff), T_series/T_parallel = √(k_parallel/k_series) = 3/√2.

working:
$k_1=3k$, $k_2=3k/2$; $k_s=(1/k_1+1/k_2)^{-1}=k$, $k_p=k_1+k_2=9k/2$. $T_s/T_p=\sqrt{k_p/k_s}=3/\sqrt{2}$.

Independent check: For a uniform spring, stiffness is inversely proportional to length, so the pieces have constants 3k and 3k/2. Thus k_series = k and k_parallel = 9k/2. Since T = 2π√(m/k_eff), T_series/T_parallel = √(k_parallel/k_series) = 3/√2.
solution:
For a uniform spring, stiffness is inversely proportional to length, so $k_1=3k$ and $k_2=3k/2$.
$$k_s=\left(\frac1{k_1}+\frac1{k_2}\right)^{-1}=k,\qquad k_p=k_1+k_2=\frac{9k}{2}$$
Since $T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k_{\text{eff}}}$, $
\frac{T_{\text{series}}}{T_{\text{parallel}}}=\sqrt{\frac{k_p}{k_s}}=\boxed{\frac{3}{\sqrt2}}$.
